newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strikes disrupt transport in two French cities.
newsitem.headline: Strikes disrupt transport in two French cities.

text.p: French tram and bus drivers went on strike on Wednesday, disrupting public transport in two major French cities to press their demands for safer and better working conditions.
Tram drivers in Toulouse, southern France, went on strike for the second day in a row over demands for retirement at 55, better conditions and a shorter working week.
Unions in the central city of Lyon, France's second city, went on strike to protest about safety after two bus drivers were assaulted in as many days.
In Toulouse, workers in the Communist-led CGT, Socialist-backed CFDT and independent FO unions blocked access to the city's two bus depots.
The unions have described the strike as "unlimited" and say they are voting each day on whether to continue their action.
Union leaders were due to meet representatives from the Toulouse public transport authority during the day.
In Lyon, the strike was triggered by anger over what unions say is a rising tide of assaults against transport workers.
"Since the beginning of the year, we have had more than 100 assaults," said CFDT representative Jean-Claude Robert.
The union said just 10 percent of the city's buses were running. Transport authorities said three of four metro lines were stopped and 22 percent of buses were in service.
